method: Same AI, separate source-first pass after freezing. Reconstructed the ordinary Mathematics degree from Annex H and reviewed 2026–2027 course content and prior knowledge, programme slots and thesis guidance. findings: The OER identifies an ordinary Mathematics major of 135 EC and a separate Mathematics and Applications programme. This generic target uses the ordinary degree. Nine compulsory 7.5 EC courses and the 15 EC thesis total 82.5 EC. ODE/PDE Modelling is the selected 7.5 EC modelling course. Discrete Mathematics and Differential Equations total 15 EC restricted choice. The 30 EC mathematics choices are Mathematics Laboratory, Numerical Mathematics, Multivariable Analysis and Differentiable Manifolds. The regulation permits Numerical Mathematics as a further mathematics choice when it is not counted in restricted choice. The remaining 45 EC are genuine profiling, with at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3. The chosen major contains 37.5 EC at level 3 (modelling, discrete mathematics, manifolds and thesis), above the 30 EC minimum. The first year is mainly Dutch, with transition toward English in the later years.

Year one pairs proofs with calculus and linear algebra in period 1, then the second calculus and linear algebra course with programming in period 2. Analysis and Mathematics Laboratory are in period 3, with groups and rings and probability in period 4. The 2026 planner lists the follow-on multivariable introduction in Year 2 period 1, topology in period 2, Differential Equations and Numerical Mathematics in period 3, and Multivariable Analysis in period 4. Differential Equations uses the prior calculus and analysis; Numerical Mathematics uses prior calculus and linear algebra. Their programme slots B and A are distinct. Year 2 has 37.5 EC of selected courses plus 22.5 EC profiling. Year 3 places Manifolds (slot A) and ODE/PDE Modelling (slot D) together in period 1 after the relevant preparation, Discrete Mathematics in period 3 and the thesis in the second semester after the main mathematics sequence. The thesis guidance provides both semester windows and asks for enough major preparation for advanced work. Year 3 has 37.5 EC of selected courses plus 22.5 EC profiling. The year-three sequence follows the current period pattern with future offerings subject to actual schedules.

The closest option builds quantitative foundations through calculus, linear algebra, numerical analysis, probability, programming and statistics. Algorithms and robotics apply discrete methods and kinematics, with linear-system and data-model work. Database Management Systems and AI Ethics replace vision and early reinforcement learning in this option, supporting computational data organisation and accountability after the introductory programming term. This preserves rigorous applied work without implying a complete proof, algebra or topology sequence. The Earth-systems option uses the same core mathematical methods in geochemical, spatial and energy contexts. Earth Observation applies remote sensing and image analysis to environmental data and Energy & Sustainability gives quantitative preparation for renewable-system design. Earth System Science Tools has direct systems and proxy analysis on its description; it follows Sustainability Essentials I, with separate geology later. The Economics option combines calculus, probability, econometrics and modelling with public economics, finance and strategic decisions. Mathematical modelling and optimisation complement, rather than constitute, dedicated financial mathematics. Description-only Advanced Calculus, Econometrics, Database Management Systems, Reinforcement Learning, Earth System Science Tools, Renewable System Design and Earth’s Resources contribute substantially within their described topics. The selected plans are distinct by the course comparisons below. The life sciences and history directions have evidence but were considered after the three stronger feasible choices. Utrecht’s proof, abstract algebra, topology, later proof-based analysis, manifolds, and mathematics research stay visible as separate requirements. Numerical approximation and multivariable calculus are bounded substantive matches. The optional UCR research row is comparison-only.
